abstract: Ising machines offer a promising route to solving NP-hard combinatorial optimization problems by mapping them onto the ground state of the Ising model. Free-space optical implementations are attractive for their inherent parallelism, scalability, and energy efficiency, yet nearly all rely on individual, sequential spin updates, leaving most of this parallelism unexploited. Here, we reclaim it with a free-space optical analog Ising machine built from off-the-shelf components in which every spin is addressed in parallel and read out in a single camera shot, while letting the system evolve under analog dynamics rather than being written and read one spin at a time. We demonstrate this architecture with over 100,000 spins, the largest spatially multiplexed analog Ising machine reported to date, with a realistic path beyond one million spins limited only by spatial-light-modulator and camera resolution. Across sparse and dense MaxCut and fully connected number-partitioning instances, our machine matches state-of-the-art solution quality. Because every spin updates in parallel, throughput increases with system size, unlike time-multiplexed machines, which slow as problems grow. The same free-space geometry also lets us solve more than 50 problem instances simultaneously, further boosting throughput. Together, these results mark an important step towards a scalable, and energy-efficient Ising machine.
